name: Rand Hall, Cornell, c. 2005: 2-D sheet, iterations 1 to 7 (AI draft)

items.text: RAND HALL (1911, Gibb & Waltz). Three-story yellow-brick daylight-factory shop building; architecture studios in the 2000s. Footprint about 200 x 52 ft (assumed from 32,915 gsf over 3 floors and the 50 ft span).
Sibley Hall (architecture, AAP), dome at its middle
Gap between Foundry, Sibley and Rand: later the site of Milstein Hall (OMA, 2011). Open in the 2000s.
ITERATION 1: SITE AND FOOTPRINT. Drawn at 1/4 of the sheet scale. Schematic from published descriptions: north-east corner of the Arts Quad, behind Sibley, along University Ave. Not surveyed.

ITERATION 2: STRUCTURAL GRID AND FIRST FLOOR PLAN (1/4"=1'-0"). 10 bays at 20 ft (assumed) between brick piers; one line of steel columns on grid B; stairs at both ends; doors in the end walls (assumed). Use in the 2000s: shop and review space (assumed).
Shop / review space (assumed). Open floor, steel columns at 20 ft.
Steel sash, full bay between piers
ITERATION 3: THIRD FLOOR, ARCHITECTURE STUDIOS (1/4"=1'-0"). Open studio floor under the sawtooth roof; desks drawn schematic, about 140 places; pin-up wall on grid B (assumed).
Studio desks, 3 x 5 ft, four to a bay (schematic)
Pin-up / crit wall between the columns (assumed)
Third floor and roof removed in the 2017-19 renovation (Ochshorn)

ITERATION 4: ROOF PLAN (1/4"=1'-0"). Sawtooth roof inside a brick parapet: four teeth of about 12'-6", ridges running east-west, vertical glazing facing north (count, pitch and direction assumed; Architectural Record confirms a sawtooth). Section A cuts mid-bay.
Roof slopes up to the north on each tooth
ITERATION 5: SOUTH ELEVATION, FIRST PASS (1/4"=1'-0"). Massing only: 200 ft long, ~43 ft to the parapet, three floors, ten full-bay openings a floor. Faces Sibley Hall across the service gap.
Steel daylight-factory sash: three units an opening, panes about 1'-6" x 1'-6", a pivoting vent in the middle unit (pane count assumed)
Light stone: water table, sill bands, cornice band, coping
Sawtooth ridge just over the parapet (assumed)
ITERATION 6: SOUTH ELEVATION, SECOND PASS (1/4"=1'-0"). Piers, stone bands, brick spandrels and the steel sash drawn. This is the face chosen for the isometric.
EAST ELEVATION (1/4"=1'-0"). Three openings wide on two piers and a centre pier; entry doors in the south bay (assumed); the sawtooth profile shows over the parapet.
Sawtooth ends, glass facing north (to the right)
3rd floor studio, lit from the north-facing sawtooth glass
Steel column on grid B, steel beams under concrete slabs (sizes assumed)
Brick bearing piers and spandrels, steel sash
SECTION A, LOOKING WEST (1/4"=1'-0"). The space Tschapeller later opened to a ~40 ft volume by taking out the third floor and roof.
ITERATION 7: EAST ELEVATION AND CROSS SECTION A.
